questions.question: According to the text, what is the primary purpose of using a correlation‑based analysis method in the context of anomaly detection?

options.A: To directly identify outlier instances in the dataset
options.B: To filter out statistically irrelevant or weakly relevant attributes before mining
options.C: To generate classification rules for distinguishing normal and anomalous data
options.D: To compute the likelihood of each data point being an outlier

questions.explanation:
The correlation‑based analysis method is described as a way to perform attribute relevance analysis and filter out statistically irrelevant or weakly relevant attributes from the descriptive mining process [Page 86].

---

questions.question: How does the text describe the relationship between outlier detection and novelty detection?

options.A: They are unrelated techniques used for different types of data
options.B: Novelty detection is a subset of outlier detection that only works on labeled data
options.C: They share similarity in modeling and detection methods because novel topics may first appear as outliers
options.D: Outlier detection always requires supervised learning, whereas novelty detection is unsupervised

questions.explanation:
The passage notes that “novel topics may initially appear as outliers” and that outlier detection and novelty detection share some similarity in modeling and detection methods [Page 101].

---

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why the choice of a deviation measurement is critical for detecting global outliers?

options.A: Because the measurement determines the dimensionality of the data representation
options.B: Because it directly influences how far a point must be from the majority to be flagged as an outlier
options.C: Because it sets the threshold for the number of clusters the algorithm will create
options.D: Because it decides whether bitmap indexing can be applied efficiently

questions.explanation:
Detecting global outliers requires an appropriate measurement of deviation; this measurement defines what constitutes sufficient deviation to label a point as an outlier [Page 101].

---

questions.question: In the classification‑based approach to anomaly detection, what prerequisite is explicitly required according to the text?

options.A: A high‑cardinality domain for bitmap indexing
options.B: A set of pre‑computed correlation coefficients among attributes
options.C: A training data set that includes class labels distinguishing normal and outlier instances
options.D: An unsupervised clustering algorithm to generate pseudo‑labels

questions.explanation:
The classification‑based method treats outlier detection as a classification problem and requires a training data set with class labels to distinguish normal data from outliers [Page 127].

---

questions.question: Based on the context, which statement correctly contrasts classification‑based and correlation‑based approaches for anomaly detection?

options.A: Classification‑based methods rely on attribute relevance analysis, while correlation‑based methods build predictive models.
options.B: Classification‑based methods need labeled data; correlation‑based methods focus on filtering irrelevant attributes without requiring labels.
options.C: Both methods require bitmap indexing to operate efficiently on low‑cardinality domains.
options.D: Classification‑based methods are used only for novelty detection, whereas correlation‑based methods are exclusive to global outlier detection.

questions.explanation:
Classification‑based approaches need labeled training data, whereas correlation‑based analysis is employed to filter out statistically irrelevant attributes, a process that does not depend on class labels [Pages 127, 86].

---

questions.question: Why might attribute‑oriented induction be considered less suitable for detailed anomaly analysis, according to the passage?

options.A: It cannot handle low‑cardinality domains efficiently
options.B: It automatically generalizes data to a higher level, limiting deep drill‑down into finer details
options.C: It requires explicit outlier labels for training a classifier
options.D: It relies exclusively on bitmap indexing, which is unsuitable for anomaly detection

questions.explanation:
Attribute‑oriented induction automatically generalizes data to a higher level, which hampers the ability to drill down to deeper, more detailed levels that may be needed for thorough anomaly analysis [Page 96].

questions.question: Which of the following best summarizes the main categorization criterion for outlier detection methods mentioned in the text?

options.A: The type of indexing structure (bitmap vs. hash) used for storage
options.B: The underlying measurement of deviation applied to the data
options.C: The presence or absence of a training phase using class labels
options.D: The cardinality of the domain on which the method operates

questions.explanation:
Outlier detection methods are partitioned into different categories based on the various measurements of deviation proposed for the application [Page 101].

questions.question: According to the excerpt, what is a common initial characteristic of novel topics that makes them detectable by outlier detection techniques?

options.A: They always have high cardinality in the attribute space
options.B: They appear as data points that deviate significantly from existing patterns
options.C: They are pre‑labeled as anomalies in the training set
options.D: They require bitmap indexing for efficient processing

questions.explanation:
Novel topics may initially appear as outliers because they deviate from previously observed data patterns, allowing outlier detection methods to identify them [Page 101].

---

questions.question: How does the text justify the need for “appropriate measurement of deviation” before applying outlier detection?

options.A: Because it determines whether bitmap indexing can be used
options.B: Because different applications may define “outlier” differently, affecting detection performance
options.C: Because it sets the number of clusters the algorithm must generate
options.D: Because it is required for constructing a correlation matrix among attributes

questions.explanation:
The passage highlights that finding an appropriate measurement of deviation is critical because it must align with the specific application’s definition of what constitutes an outlier [Page 101].

questions.question: Which statement accurately reflects the scope of outlier detection methods discussed in the chapter, as indicated by the text?

options.A: The chapter only covers statistical likelihood approaches for anomaly detection.
options.B: It includes a discussion of multiple categories, such as global outlier detection, classification‑based methods, and correlation‑based attribute filtering.
options.C: It focuses exclusively on bitmap indexing techniques for low‑cardinality domains.
options.D: The chapter argues that outlier detection is unrelated to novelty detection.

questions.explanation: The text mentions various outlier detection categories, including measurement‑based methods, classification‑based approaches, and correlation‑based attribute relevance analysis, indicating a broad discussion of multiple methods [Pages 101, 105, 127, 86].
